title: Publisher subpath and clean runtime-smoke shutdown hardening

findings.publisher_subpath_bug: The package-root app.py did not forward the framework root_path contract, so a company reverse proxy that mounts the app under a path such as /visualizer could reach the server as GET /visualizer and receive 404.
findings.smoke_shutdown_bug: runtime_smoke intentionally sent SIGINT to its own child server, which can surface asyncio.CancelledError followed by KeyboardInterrupt on Python 3.13 even though the user did not cancel the smoke run.

changes: app.py resolves COMPANY_UI_ROOT_PATH plus common ROOT_PATH, SCRIPT_NAME, APPLICATION_ROOT and MOUNT_PATH publisher variables.
The exact existing live-lab runtime receives root_path; no project-specific route alias was added.
live_lab_cli exposes --root-path for deterministic manual verification.
runtime_smoke stops its server with graceful terminate/SIGTERM and escalates only to kill; it never synthesizes SIGINT.
The 22-route golden-template authority is frozen by regression coverage.

regression_evidence.browser_uiux_baseline: 46/46 PASS unchanged; no renderer or CSS change

target_action: On the company target, rerun ./setup.sh. If the publisher externally mounts this app below a subpath and does not export one automatically, set COMPANY_UI_ROOT_PATH to that exact mount prefix (for example /visualizer).
